title: Passive flexion torque of the intact torso vs the osteoligamentous lumbar spine, as % of the in vivo elastic limit

quantity.name: flexion torque vs % of in vivo elastic limit
quantity.definition: torque (Nm) of the intact torso (this study, flexion fit) and of the osteoligamentous spine (Adams & Dolan 1991 in vivo/in vitro relation) plotted against % of the in vivo flexion elastic limit; the difference is attributed to passive tissues other than disc and ligaments (muscle, skin, viscera)

source.authors: McGill S, Seguin J, Bennett G
source.sample: 22 male + 15 female undergraduates, no disabling LBP in the previous year

protocol.summary: Flexion/extension: side-lying; lateral bend: supine. Pelvis and lower body strapped to a fixed jig, upper torso (top of head to ~T12) strapped in a 'floating' cradle on precision nylon ball bearings over glass (no resistance to planar translation/rotation); scissor jacks aligned the spine in neutral, foam cushions under waist/knees when needed. Bending moment applied to the cradle by a cable kept normal to the cradle (load cell); moment = force x perpendicular distance to the lateral iliac crest (~L4/L5). Axial rotation: upright standing, rib cage fixed by a restraining harness, torque applied to a rotating platform under the feet. Angle = rib cage (3-SPACE Isotrak sensor over xiphoid) relative to pelvis (source strapped to pelvis), accuracy +-0.3 deg. Audio EMG biofeedback (bilateral L3 erector spinae and external oblique) to relax; trials with prolonged EMG repeated. Torque ramped over ~10 s (peak at 7-8 s) until the subject's tolerance limit. 3 trials x 6 directions (flexion, extension, CW twist, CCW twist, right and left lateral bend) x 3 conditions (normal, held breath at maximal inhalation, leather lifting belt 11 cm posterior / 6.5 cm anterior); condition order fixed (normal, breath hold, belt). Mean raw torque-angle data per sex, direction and condition fitted with T = lambda*exp(beta*alpha) (T in Nm, alpha in deg) from 0 Nm up to the torque still tolerated by half the subjects. Fig 6: the authors converted the intact-torso flexion data to % of the in vivo elastic limit using the Adams & Dolan (1991) equations and overlaid the osteoligamentous curve.
how_to_simulate: Side-lying passive flexion, pelvis fixed, zero muscle activation; express lumbar flexion as % of the model's in vivo elastic (end-range) flexion limit
Report the total passive moment and the part carried by the osteoligamentous structures (discs + ligaments + facets) separately
Compare the total with the intact-torso curve and the difference (non-ligamentous passive tissues) with the derived series

subject_model.source: Table 1 male means (female cohort: 20.8 y, 164.8 cm, 62.3 kg)

protocol.notes: Shape comparison only: both curves are converted/derived by the authors (the osteoligamentous curve is from another study). The flat line at ~0 Nm in Fig 6 is the x-axis. Authors' conclusion: non-ligamentous tissues add < ~6 Nm over the mid range.

extraction.check_notes: Digitised by pixel column scans of a 300 dpi render at the printed x ticks (0/25/50/75/100%) against the y tick marks (25, 20, 15, 10 Nm at 382, 445, 507, 570 px; zero taken at the x-axis line ~692 px). Both curves meet at 100% (~21.7 Nm). Osteoligamentous value at 25% is within line width of zero.

pass_rule.rule: shape check: model total passive flexion moment above the osteoligamentous moment at 25-75% of the elastic limit and converging at end range; values within +-30% of the intact-torso curve
